name: Hana Costa

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I’m with the Work Futures Panel, an independent research group with no ties to employers, AI companies, unions, political parties or government. We sell nothing and campaign for no side. This is confidential. Tell me what an ordinary day at the contact centre is like.

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I’m 43 and still junior on the call and chat desk. I finished secondary school and earn about the usual rate for this job. I am slower than other agents with mixed payment cases, so I ask an experienced colleague before closing one. I do not use AI tools; a draft I cannot explain to a customer does not help me.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: What part of that day stays with you after work?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: My partner, Paolo, and I have two children in school and a mortgage. We have around four months of expenses saved, and there are some other centres within reach. Paolo works at a building supply shop. I like the regular customers who remember my voice. I do not like finishing a call without knowing what happened to their payment.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d tell the desk AI Plateau leaves the phone line much as it is. If a draft fills a note faster, I still want an agent to read the payment record before closing the case.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think my job remains, but I have a mortgage and two children to feed. Four months saved helps me sleep, though I would not spend it on a new device I do not understand.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I’d keep the same calls and ask Sera, the agent beside me, to check mixed payments before I close them. In the first year of small change, I’d add a fixed amount from each pay to the reserve and keep using the account record rather than an AI tool.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Calm about the work, uneasy about ordinary bills. Four months of savings is a cushion for my mortgage, not a reason to stop checking costs.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Which payment would you double-check?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A customer once paid half a bill on one date and half on another. I nearly read only the second line, but Sera (my colleague) pointed me back to the full history.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why keep adding to savings?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Paolo (my partner) and I keep the reserve in a separate account. I would add to it after payday before we discuss a weekend outing.

say: I’d say **phone calls** still need an agent who reads the record.
I’d ask colleagues to check **mixed payments** before closing them.
think: I think my **job remains** in this mild change.
I still watch **mortgage costs** with children at home.
do: Keep **taking calls** and checking mixed payments with Sera in 2026.
Add a **fixed amount** to the reserve during the first year.
feel: **Calm** about work, uneasy about household bills.
S0.quote: Four months of savings is a cushion for my mortgage, not a reason to stop checking costs.
fieldNote: Her **four-month reserve** softens current mortgage worry.
She relies on **Sera’s experience** for difficult mixed payments.
She does not adopt **AI tools** merely for a small time saving.

steps.text: Keep answering calls and checking mixed payments with an experienced agent
Add a fixed amount from each pay to the mortgage reserve

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d tell colleagues Steady Disruption will take routine billing chats first. I would ask management whether junior hours will be cut or whether we can practise difficult calls on paid shifts.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think my hours could shrink because I am not yet quick on the disputes that might remain. There are other centres nearby, but they may use the same system and I cannot gamble the mortgage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I’d keep notes on disputed bills I help solve and ask for one paid difficult-case shift monthly with Sera if offered. In the first year routine chats move, I’d apply for a posted customer desk role nearby only if its written hours and wage cover our mortgage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious. I am willing to learn a real job beside someone, but I do not want a screen telling me I am ready after a short test.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How would Sera help?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask Sera (my colleague) to show me one wrong fee and one missing payment on a paid shift. I could practise the record, not just watch a demonstration.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you take another centre’s offer?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would take another centre’s job only after seeing written hours and a wage that keeps the house paid. Paolo (my partner) and I can discuss a route then.

say: I’d ask whether **junior paid hours** will fall as routine billing chats move.
I’d request **paid difficult-call practice** before the chats move.
think: I think my **hours could shrink** when routine billing leaves.
I doubt **nearby centres** are automatically safe for the mortgage.
do: Record **solved bills** and take paid practice with Sera if offered.
Seek **posted desk work** with written mortgage-covering hours and wages.
S1.quote: I am willing to learn a real job beside someone, but I do not want a screen telling me I am ready after a short test.
fieldNote: She favours **paid side-by-side practice** over a screen demonstration.
Her **junior standing** makes routine-chat automation a direct threat.
She wants **written hours and wage** before moving centres.

steps.text: Take one paid difficult-case shift monthly beside Sera if offered
Apply for a posted nearby desk job with written mortgage-covering hours and wage

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say AGI by 2028 could take the calls and the careful checks too. I would ask the centre for written notice and the names of paid posts that will still be there.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think my headset work could end in 2028, three years before robots arrive. Four months saved would run down quickly with a mortgage, even if Paolo keeps his shop hours.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I’d hold off replacing the dining table and ask for a written staffing date. In the first year after 2028, I’d apply for a posted paid reception job only if its hours cover the mortgage; I would take funded training only if required for that named opening.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Alarmed. The mortgage is due before any robot reaches the contact centre.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you tell Paolo about the table?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell Paolo (my partner) the table can last another year. It is scratched, not broken, and keeping the money for the mortgage is the sensible choice.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would make training real?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask for the vacancy, wage and paid training hours in writing. If the company only offers a course without a job, I would keep looking at the other centres.

say: I’d ask management for **written notice** and the names of paid posts that remain.
I’d say **2028 thinking AI** reaches calls before robots.
think: I think my **headset work could end** in 2028.
I know **four months saved** would shrink quickly under the mortgage.
do: Defer the **table purchase** and seek staffing dates in 2026.
Apply for **posted reception work** after 2028 only with written wages and hours covering the mortgage.
Take **funded training** only if required for that named opening, with paid study hours.
S2.quote: The mortgage is due before any robot reaches the contact centre.
fieldNote: She correctly separates **2028 thinking work** from 2031 robots.
The **table delay** protects liquid mortgage money.
She requires a **named vacancy** before funded training.
She would keep looking at **other centres** if offered only a course.

steps.text: Keep the scratched dining table another year to protect mortgage money
Apply for posted reception work with written mortgage-covering wages and hours after 2028
Take funded training with paid study hours only if the named opening requires it

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say AGI by 2031 gives time for the centre to teach people on paid shifts, not just send a course link. I would ask for posted roles with wages before anyone changes jobs.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think five years could let me learn disputed payments properly, though I still expect fewer phone agents after AGI. Paolo’s shop income and our four months saved help, but neither replaces my wage forever.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: From 2026 I’d take one paid difficult-bill shift monthly with Sera if the centre offers it and save part of each pay. In the first year after 2031, I’d apply for a posted billing role with written mortgage-covering hours and take an employer-funded course only if required for that job.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious, with enough time to make a careful move. I want a paid shift beside my colleague Sera before I pay for any course.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would Sera show you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask Sera (my colleague) to let me work through a missing payment while she watches. If I get it wrong, she can show me the line I missed before a customer hears it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you leave town for work?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would show Paolo (my partner) the posted job and wage before spending our savings on any move. Our children are settled in school, so a better title alone would not pull us away.

say: I’d ask for **posted billing roles** with real wages before people enroll in courses.
I’d ask for **paid teaching shifts** before course links.
think: I think I could master **disputed payments** over five years.
I still expect **fewer phone agents** after 2031.
do: Take **paid difficult-bill shifts** if offered and save from each pay.
Apply for **posted billing work** after 2031 with written mortgage-covering hours and stated wages.
Take an **employer-funded course** only if required for that posted job.
S3.quote: I want a paid shift beside my colleague Sera before I pay for any course.
fieldNote: Her **paid practice** is concrete work on missing payments.
She protects the **reserve** against a course without a vacancy.
The **children’s school** raises the cost of an unnecessary move.

steps.text: Take a monthly paid missing-payment shift beside Sera if offered
Save part of each pay toward the mortgage reserve
Apply for posted billing work with written mortgage-covering hours and stated wages after 2031
Take an employer-funded course only if required for that posted billing job

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say AGI by 2036 gives us a decade to build savings and teach junior agents properly. I would ask the centre to keep paid first shifts where someone can learn beside an experienced person.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think I could be steadier at this job by 53, but thinking AI may still take phone work in 2036. Robots around 2039 come after that, and our mortgage still needs a payment each month.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I’d keep taking calls, save a fixed part of each pay and ask for paid difficult-case shifts if offered. In the first year after 2036, I’d apply for a posted staffed billing role only if my hours fall and its written wage covers the mortgage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Uneasy about the end point and mindful of next month’s payment. Ten years before AGI in 2036 is time to prepare, not time off from the mortgage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you practise?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would take one missing-payment case a month on a paid shift with Sera if the centre agreed. I can get better at a job I know without chasing a new tool every week.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would the family move?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep the children in their school unless Paolo (my partner) and I had a signed offer and a workable route. A title in another town would not be enough.

I’d say a decade allows **saving and teaching** before AGI.

I know **2036 thinking AI** could still take phone work.
do: Keep **taking calls**, save each pay and take paid practice if offered.
Apply for **posted billing work** after 2036 only if hours fall and wages cover mortgage.
feel: **Uneasy** about the endpoint and present mortgage.
S4.quote: Ten years before AGI in 2036 is time to prepare, not time off from the mortgage.
fieldNote: She prefers **paid experience** over frequent tool changes.
A move requires a **signed offer** and school route.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because my calls and chat checks are thinking work, and four months of savings cannot hold our mortgage for long. A written notice period, a real paid vacancy with enough hours, and learning beside an experienced worker on paid time would help.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn’t ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: You did not ask who takes the first call from a confused customer. I learned customer service because a senior agent sat beside me and let me ask a simple question without shame.

headlineQuote: I learned customer service because a senior agent sat beside me and let me ask a simple question without shame.
portrait: At **43**, Hana is a junior customer agent after secondary school, still slow on mixed payment cases.
She and Paolo support **two schoolchildren** and a mortgage with four months of expenses saved.
She avoids **AI tools** and prefers to check payment records with an experienced colleague.
She would protect the **household reserve** and move only for written paid work.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could remove her screen work before four months of savings buys a safe move.
whatWouldHelp: **Written notice**, a posted mortgage-covering role and paid learning beside an agent would help.
